renderPacket.identity: ONE SINGLE FULL-BLEED 3:2 WIDE LANDSCAPE FRAME of the real Kampong Ayer water village on the Brunei River in Bandar Seri Begawan, seen from low river level as if from a moving water taxi in calm late-afternoon light. Recognisable timber and modern stilt houses on piles and connected walkways occupy the middle distance; the broad brown-green tropical river remains clearly visible. Across/beyond the water village, include the real golden dome and slender minaret silhouette of Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque only where geographically plausible, small enough to remain background context rather than a separate landmark portrait. Keep the main visual anchor centre-right so the left side retains calmer river/sky negative space for Hero text. Humid equatorial atmosphere, restrained tropical greens, warm gold accents, realistic Brunei architecture and proportions, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4, refined travel-atlas painterly realism. No fantasy palace, no invented skyline, no Jame’ ‘Asr mosque substitution, no composite of unrelated landmarks.

Real Jame’ ‘Asr Hassanil Bolkiah Mosque in Bandar Seri Begawan, viewed from the formal garden/approach so the mosque's distinctive multiple golden domes, pale stone walls, minarets and landscaped foreground are recognisable together. Soft clear morning or late-afternoon tropical light, realistic proportions and symmetry, a few small visitors only if natural, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. This is the Jame’ ‘Asr mosque, not Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque, and not a generic fantasy mosque.

Real Ulu Temburong National Park rainforest in eastern Brunei, viewed from the elevated canopy walkway/tower over dense layered Bornean rainforest. The forest canopy must dominate, with ridges fading into humid distance and only a restrained section of the real steel canopy structure as a location cue. Early morning mist or soft daylight, biologically plausible lowland/hill tropical forest, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. No giant fantasy suspension bridge, no waterfall montage, no generic jungle resort.

Real Sultan Haji Omar ‘Ali Saifuddien Bridge crossing Brunei Bay, a long low modern roadway sweeping across broad tidal water toward Temburong, viewed obliquely from an elevated but plausible shoreline/bay perspective. Emphasise the unusual scale and continuity of the bridge against mangrove-fringed tropical water, with bridge towers/road engineering accurately restrained. Clear humid daylight or late afternoon, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. No impossible aerial satellite view, no urban skyline composite, no dramatic fantasy suspension bridge.

Real Tasek Merimbun in Tutong District, Brunei: calm dark tea-black water reflecting tropical forest and wetland vegetation, low wooded shores and a quiet natural-lake scale. View from near water level or a simple lakeside viewpoint, soft overcast or early-morning light that makes the blackwater character visible without turning the lake unnaturally black. Photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. No mountain lake, no turquoise water, no resort structures, no fantasy swamp.

Real Billionth Barrel Monument area on the coast at Seria, Brunei, seen as one coherent coastal landscape: the recognisable arched monument at natural scale with open South China Sea horizon and restrained oil-field infrastructure/pumpjacks visible in the wider setting where plausible. Warm late-afternoon coastal light, sandy/grass foreground, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. Keep it documentary and geographic, not an industrial poster; no refinery skyline invented behind the monument.

Real Tamu Kianggeh market beside the Kianggeh River in Bandar Seri Begawan during an ordinary morning. One continuous human-scale market view with modest covered stalls, tropical produce and local food, shoppers and vendors naturally distributed, and a glimpse of the river/green bank anchoring the riverside setting. Soft tropical morning light, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. No staged bazaar fantasy, no oversized food still life, no readable generated signage.

Real Teraja Iban longhouse in the Labi area of Belait District, Brunei, viewed from outside at human eye level so the extended raised communal timber structure, veranda and forest-edge setting read as one inhabited place. Include only small natural signs of daily life; architecture and relationship to surrounding tropical forest are the focus. Soft morning daylight, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. No generic tribal village, no ceremonial crowd, no invented Borneo fantasy architecture.

Real Muara Beach on Brunei's South China Sea coast: broad pale sandy beach, calm-to-moderate tropical sea, low coastal vegetation and casuarina/palm greenery, with a few small local families or walkers only if natural. Wide open horizon and everyday public-beach atmosphere in clear late-afternoon light, photo 6 : quiet watercolor 4. No luxury resort, no Maldives-style turquoise lagoon exaggeration, no dramatic cliffs or invented islands.

Exactly one Bruneian ambuyat serving as the single food subject: one simple ceramic bowl containing translucent glossy sago starch paste, centred and large on a completely plain warm ivory or pale beige seamless background. A pair of candas may rest naturally at the rim as the only eating utensil if needed for identity. Do not add separate cacah bowls, side dishes, rice, vegetables, raw ingredients, drinks, table setting or decorative props.

Exactly one Bruneian nasi katok dish on one simple plate, centred and large against a completely plain warm ivory or pale beige seamless background: a compact mound of white rice, one piece of golden fried chicken and a small portion of red sambal on the same plate. No second plate, no extra bowls, no soup, no cucumber/garnish pile, no cutlery, raw ingredients, drink, restaurant or kitchen setting.

Exactly one Bruneian kelupis serving as the single dish: several short compact parcels of steamed glutinous rice wrapped in pale-green daun nyirik/leaf wrappers, arranged together on one simple plate, with one parcel partly opened only if needed to show the white sticky rice texture. Completely plain warm ivory or pale beige seamless background. No curry, satay, sauce bowls, extra side dishes, cutlery, raw leaves scattered around, drink or decorative props.

Exactly one Bruneian penyaram serving as the single dish: several small round deep-fried brown rice-flour cakes with characteristic thicker domed centres and thinner crinkled edges, arranged together on one simple plate, centred and large against a completely plain warm ivory or pale beige seamless background. No second sweets, fruit, sauce, utensils, raw ingredients, drinks or decorative props.
